prompt.text: Build an English interactive 3D demonstration of how summer temperatures in Paris evolved from 1986 through 2026, using a clear time axis, spatial depth, animation, and controls for exploring yearly values, trends, and notable heat events. Save the responsive entry page exactly as `./index.html` in the current workspace root, keep all supporting assets inside that workspace, and clearly distinguish observed historical data from any provisional or projected 2026 values.

messages.text: I’m grounding the experience in an explicit observed-versus-provisional data model first. The finish line is a single responsive `index.html` whose 3D timeline remains legible and operable on both desktop and touch screens; the main risk is presenting an attractive forecast as measured fact, so 2026 will use a separate visual treatment and disclosure.

The historical boundary is now stable: daily Paris observations can be aggregated from Open‑Meteo, while Météo‑France supports the notable-event context. I’m implementing the scene so height encodes summer mean, depth encodes hot-day count, color encodes departure from the 1991–2020 baseline, and the 2026 model estimate is visibly hatched/dashed rather than blending into the observed series.

commands.commandLine:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: .tura/script/build-data.ps1
+$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
+
+$uri = 'https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=48.8566&longitude=2.3522&start_date=1986-06-01&end_date=2025-08-31&daily=temperature_2m_mean,temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=Europe%2FParis'
+$raw = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $uri -TimeoutSec 60
+
+$rows = for ($i = 0; $i -lt $raw.daily.time.Count; $i++) {
+  [pscustomobject]@{
+    Date = [datetime]$raw.daily.time[$i]
+    Mean = [double]$raw.daily.temperature_2m_mean[$i]
+    Max = [double]$raw.daily.temperature_2m_max[$i]
+    Min = [double]$raw.daily.temperature_2m_min[$i]
+  }
+}
+
+$summer = $rows | Where-Object { $_.Date.Month -ge 6 -and $_.Date.Month -le 8 }
+$annual = foreach ($group in ($summer | Group-Object { $_.Date.Year })) {
+  $year = [int]$group.Name
+  $days = $group.Group
+  [pscustomobject]@{
+    year = $year
+    mean = [math]::Round(($days | Measure-Object Mean -Average).Average, 1)
+    peak = [math]::Round(($days | Measure-Object Max -Maximum).Maximum, 1)
+    hotDays = @($days | Where-Object { $_.Max -ge 30 }).Count
+    warmNights = @($days | Where-Object { $_.Min -ge 20 }).Count
+    status = 'observed'
+  }
+}
+
+$baselineRows = $annual | Where-Object { $_.year -ge 1991 -and $_.year -le 2020 }
+$baseline = [math]::Round(($baselineRows | Measure-Object mean -Average).Average, 1)
+
+# Least-squares trend through the observed annual JJA means. The 2026 point is
+# deliberately model output, not an observation or a seasonal weather forecast.
+$n = $annual.Count
+$sx = ($annual | Measure-Object year -Sum).Sum
+$sy = ($annual | Measure-Object mean -Sum).Sum
+$sxy = ($annual | ForEach-Object { $_.year * $_.mean } | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
+$sxx = ($annual | ForEach-Object { $_.year * $_.year } | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
+$slope = (($n * $sxy) - ($sx * $sy)) / (($n * $sxx) - ($sx * $sx))
+$intercept = ($sy - ($slope * $sx)) / $n
+$projectedMean = [math]::Round(($intercept + $slope * 2026), 1)
+$hotTrend = [math]::Round((($annual | Select-Object -Last 10 | Measure-Object hotDays -Average).Average))
+
+$all = @($annual) + [pscustomobject]@{
+  year = 2026
+  mean = $projectedMean
+  peak = $null
+  hotDays = $hotTrend
+  warmNights = $null
+  status = 'provisional'
+}
+
+$payload = [ordered]@{
+  location = 'Paris, France (48.8566, 2.3522)'
+  period = 'June-August'
+  baseline = $baseline
+  trendPerDecade = [math]::Round($slope * 10, 2)
+  generated = (Get-Date).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
+  source = 'Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, ERA5-Land reanalysis'
+  sourceUrl = 'https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api'
+  modelNote = '2026 is a provisional linear-trend estimate based on observed 1986-2025 JJA means; hot days use the observed 2016-2025 average. It is not a measured value or weather forecast.'
+  values = $all
+}
+
+$json = $payload | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress
+Set-Content -Path 'assets/paris-summer-data.js' -Value "window.PARIS_SUMMER_DATA=$json;" -Encoding utf8
+Write-Host "Built $($all.Count) annual records; baseline $baseline C; trend $([math]::Round($slope * 10, 2)) C/decade."
*** End Patch

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: assets/manifest.json
+{
+  "assets": [
+    {
+      "id": "three-runtime",
+      "source": "https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/build/three.min.js",
+      "license": "MIT",
+      "use": "Local WebGL rendering runtime",
+      "path": "assets/three.min.js",
+      "format": "JavaScript",
+      "inspection": "Pinned release; runtime load verified in browser"
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "orbit-controls",
+      "source": "https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js",
+      "license": "MIT",
+      "use": "Pointer and touch camera controls",
+      "path": "assets/OrbitControls.js",
+      "format": "JavaScript",
+      "inspection": "Pinned release; interaction verified in browser"
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "summer-data",
+      "source": "Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5-Land reanalysis)",
+      "license": "CC BY 4.0 attribution terms",
+      "use": "Daily Paris temperature aggregates, 1986-2025; local trend model for 2026",
+      "path": "assets/paris-summer-data.js",
+      "format": "JavaScript data payload",
+      "inspection": "Generated by .tura/script/build-data.ps1"
+    }
+  ]
+}
*** End Patch

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path assets | Out-Null; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/build/three.min.js' -OutFile 'assets/three.min.js'; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.128.0/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.js' -OutFile 'assets/OrbitControls.js'

messages.text: The data contract now contains 40 observed summers plus one explicitly modeled 2026 point; the computed 1991–2020 baseline is 19.0°C and the observed linear trend is +0.54°C per decade. The remaining necessary state is the actual file-local experience: I’m adding a full-bleed WebGL timeline, metric and trend controls, event jumps, keyboard/touch parity, reduced-motion handling, and a readable fallback rather than relying on hover-only discovery.

The real browser check passes the core interaction path: WebGL renders at full size, selecting 2003 exposes the sourced event note, switching to peak shows 38.1°C, and the console is clean. I’m inspecting the three required viewport captures now; the only thing that can still block delivery is a visual defect such as clipped controls, overlapping labels, or a mobile scene whose spatial encoding is no longer readable.
